supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:04 UTC, the domain controller recorded a service-ticket request for ken.ito to WS-MSANTOS-01 from 10.54.10.23, which the inventory identifies as WS-KITO-01. This is consistent with possible IT activity near the reported time, but does not establish what action was performed.

At 13:42 UTC, WS-MSANTOS-01 used a Windows Update Agent connection to download about 38.8 MB from download.windowsupdate.com. This is consistent with patching activity but does not link that download to PowerShell or ken.ito.

At 13:39:42 UTC, WS-MSANTOS-01 made an SMB connection to DC-BLU-01, and the domain controller recorded a network logon for the workstation machine account. The records do not identify a share or file accessed.

The supplied endpoint process records show conhost.exe starting at 14:16:15 under SYSTEM with csrss.exe as its parent, then exiting at 14:16:57. They do not establish that this was the PowerShell window reported around 13:40.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not show a PowerShell process creation, command line, script content, or parent process for the reported time. The process events present for WS-MSANTOS-01 concern conhost.exe at 14:16, not the reported time (T184-00423, T184-00424, T184-00430, T184-00431).
The available network and authentication records do not show whether ken.ito executed a remote command or accessed the organization's patch script share.
claims_not_established: That a PowerShell process actually ran on WS-MSANTOS-01 around 13:40 UTC.
What command or script, if any, ran, and whether it was authorized workstation patching.
Whether the ken.ito service-ticket request and subsequent Windows Update download were part of the reported activity.
Whether the SMB connection to DC-BLU-01 involved any particular share or file.
additional_evidence_needed: Endpoint EDR or Windows process-creation records for WS-MSANTOS-01 around 13:40 UTC, including parent process and command line.
PowerShell operational or script-block logs, and available console history or forensic artifacts for the reported time.
SMB share-access auditing on FILE-BLU-01 to determine whether Patch-Workstations.ps1 was accessed, plus remote-execution telemetry from WS-KITO-01.
Confirmation from ken.ito and mia.santos about any patching or remote support performed at the time.
unrelated_findings: At 13:52 UTC, DC-BLU-01 initiated connections toward WS-MSANTOS-01 on ports 8443, 135, 443, and 445; some attempts were reset, unanswered, or rejected. Triage separately; these records do not establish a link to the reported PowerShell activity (T184-00300, T184-00301, T184-00309, T184-00310, T184-00312, T184-00313).

At 13:29 UTC, WS-MSANTOS-01 accessed a Citrix StoreWeb portal at customer.cloud.com. The inventory does not list this service as approved; review separately, without treating it as evidence for this alert (T184-00100, T184-00104, T184-00121).
